AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these is a green material for a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Dry leaves
   B. Fresh cut grass
   C. Straw
   D. Dry maize stalks

2. Why does drip irrigation save water? (1 mark)
   A. It uses more water than a hose
   B. It wets the paths between plants
   C. Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   D. It waters at midday

3. Why does a higher container give a faster drip? (1 mark)
   A. Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   B. It has more air
   C. It is nearer the sun
   D. It has a lid

4. What is irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Spraying crops with medicine
   B. Digging the soil
   C. Harvesting crops
   D. Giving water to crops by ways other than rain

5. What is the meaning of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Selling water
   B. Using it carefully so none is wasted
   C. Using as much as possible
   D. Storing dirty water

6. Who should make holes in bottle caps and pipes with a nail? (1 mark)
   A. A small child alone
   B. Nobody
   C. A teacher or an adult
   D. Anyone with wet hands

7. Which stove saves more charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. An improved jiko
   B. An open fire in the wind
   C. A broken pot
   D. A stone on the ground

8. What is a fuel? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of food
   B. Something we burn to get heat
   C. A cleaning tool
   D. A type of soil

9. What is used to make the arms of a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A bottle
   B. Sand
   C. A shorter stick tied across the pole
   D. A bucket of water

10. Which animal often picks maize cobs and bananas? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Duck
   C. Cow
   D. Monkey

11. Which is the safest way to make holes or dig for scarecrow parts? (1 mark)
   A. Play with the tools
   B. Ask an adult to help
   C. Use bare hands on sharp tools
   D. Use broken glass

12. Which crop is established by direct sowing of tiny seeds? (1 mark)
   A. Sweet potato
   B. Banana
   C. Carrot
   D. Mango

13. What is transplanting? (1 mark)
   A. Sowing seeds directly
   B. Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   C. Making compost
   D. Harvesting

14. Which tool gives gentle watering of a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. Cup thrown from far
   B. Watering can with a fine rose
   C. Hose without a nozzle
   D. Bucket poured fast

15. Why are carrots not transplanted? (1 mark)
   A. Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   B. They grow in water
   C. They have no roots
   D. They are too large

16. When should the grass mulch be removed? (1 mark)
   A. After harvesting
   B. When seedlings begin to appear
   C. At sowing
   D. Never

17. How fine should the soil in the seedbed be? (1 mark)
   A. Wet like mud
   B. Full of big clods
   C. Hard like stone
   D. Crumbly like brown sugar

18. How far should mulch be from the stem? (1 mark)
   A. Piled tightly against it
   B. Ten metres
   C. Not needed
   D. A small gap away

19. Which nutrient in oranges and guavas helps the body to heal cuts and fight colds? (1 mark)
   A. Cooking oil
   B. Vitamin C
   C. Salt
   D. Starch

20. Which sign shows that a guava is ripe? (1 mark)
   A. It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   B. It is dark green and hard
   C. It has flowers on it
   D. It is dry and black

21. Which nutrient do oranges and guavas supply in large amounts? (1 mark)
   A. Salt
   B. Cooking oil
   C. Vitamin C
   D. Starch

22. Which product comes from a hen? (1 mark)
   A. Honey
   B. Leather
   C. Eggs
   D. Wool

23. Which animal is not domestic? (1 mark)
   A. Hen
   B. Goat
   C. Cow
   D. Elephant

24. Which product does a dairy cow give? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Wool
   C. Milk
   D. Feathers

25. Which nutrient in milk builds strong bones and teeth? (1 mark)
   A. Sugar
   B. Salt
   C. Starch
   D. Calcium

26. Which of these fruits is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Rice
   B. Orange
   C. Butter
   D. Chapati

27. Which of these meals is balanced? (1 mark)
   A. Chips only
   B. Tea and bread only
   C. Soda and sweets
   D. Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki

28. Why is a food journal kept for a week? (1 mark)
   A. To check whether meals are balanced
   B. To count the number of plates
   C. To improve handwriting only
   D. To find cheap shops

29. Who should be with a child who is cooking? (1 mark)
   A. An adult
   B. A friend only
   C. A younger child
   D. Nobody

30. Why should potatoes be cut into pieces of equal size before boiling? (1 mark)
   A. To make them cold
   B. To make them bigger
   C. They cook at the same time
   D. To waste time

31. Which way should pot handles point? (1 mark)
   A. Outward over the floor
   B. Towards children
   C. Down into the fire
   D. Inward, away from the edge

32. Why should combs and towels not be shared? (1 mark)
   A. They break
   B. They become dirty faster
   C. Germs and lice can spread
   D. They are too big

33. What should you use to brush your teeth? (1 mark)
   A. A knife
   B. A comb
   C. A cloth soaked in oil
   D. A toothbrush and toothpaste

34. Which of these can be made into a mop? (1 mark)
   A. A shoe
   B. Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   C. A basin
   D. A chair

35. Which method wipes dust from furniture? (1 mark)
   A. Dusting
   B. Sweeping
   C. Burning
   D. Mopping

36. Which method uses water and a mop? (1 mark)
   A. Dusting
   B. Burning
   C. Sweeping
   D. Mopping

37. What is refuse? (1 mark)
   A. Food
   B. Soap
   C. Clean water
   D. Rubbish or waste

38. What should you do after cleaning the house? (1 mark)
   A. Wash hands with soap
   B. Eat without washing
   C. Touch food
   D. Play in the dirt

39. Which is a way of reducing waste? (1 mark)
   A. Reuse containers
   B. Throw things away quickly
   C. Buy more packages
   D. Burn tins

40. Why do we knot the end of the thread? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To make it stronger
   C. To colour it
   D. So it does not pull through the cloth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain four benefits of conserving fuel. (4 marks)

42. Explain how measuring skills help you in tacking. (3 marks)

43. Describe the first aid for a small burn. (3 marks)

44. Name three products we get from cattle. (3 marks)

45. Name two things that should never be put in a compost heap and say why. (2 marks)

46. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

47. Give three uses of tacking stitches. (3 marks)

48. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)

49. Describe how to clean canvas shoes. (4 marks)

50. Name the young of a cow, a goat and a sheep. (3 marks)

51. Give three reasons why fruits are important. (3 marks)

52. Describe how to make even tacking. (4 marks)

53. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)

54. Explain three safety rules when cleaning. (3 marks)

55. Explain the meaning of domestic hygiene. (2 marks)

56. Give three signs that fruit is ripe, naming the fruit. (3 marks)

57. List four safety rules when cooking. (4 marks)

58. A drip system drips very fast at one hole and not at all at another. Explain what may be wrong and how to fix each. (4 marks)

59. Why should a thread colour different from the cloth be used? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #9 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Fresh cut grass
   Green materials are fresh and wet, such as fresh grass, peelings and fresh dung.

2. C — Water goes close to the roots so little is wasted
   Only the soil near the plant is wet, so less water is lost.

3. A — Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   A higher container gives a bigger push for water flowing down.

4. D — Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   Irrigation means supplying water to crops artificially.

5. B — Using it carefully so none is wasted
   Conserving means saving and protecting.

6. C — A teacher or an adult
   Nails and awls are sharp and can cause injuries.

7. A — An improved jiko
   An improved jiko holds heat around the pot.

8. B — Something we burn to get heat
   Fuels such as wood and gas are burnt for heat.

9. C — A shorter stick tied across the pole
   The cross stick forms shoulders and arms.

10. D — Monkey
   Monkeys pick crops from farms near forests.

11. B — Ask an adult to help
   Safety comes first.

12. C — Carrot
   Carrots are sown directly because transplanting damages their roots.

13. B — Moving young plants from a nursery to the field
   Transplanting means moving seedlings.

14. B — Watering can with a fine rose
   Fine spray does not wash seeds away.

15. A — Moving damages the root and makes it crooked
   The carrot root is the food, so it must grow straight.

16. B — When seedlings begin to appear
   Seedlings need light.

17. D — Crumbly like brown sugar
   Fine crumbly soil lets seeds come up easily.

18. D — A small gap away
   Mulch touching the stem can cause rot.

19. B — Vitamin C
   Vitamin C helps the body fight illness.

20. A — It turns yellowish and smells sweet
   Ripe guavas change colour and smell sweet.

21. C — Vitamin C
   Citrus fruits and guavas are rich in vitamin C.

22. C — Eggs
   Hens lay eggs.

23. D — Elephant
   Elephants are wild.

24. C — Milk
   Dairy cows are kept for milk.

25. D — Calcium
   Milk has calcium and protein.

26. B — Orange
   Fruits are protective foods.

27. D — Ugali, beans and sukuma wiki
   It includes all three groups.

28. A — To check whether meals are balanced
   A journal shows patterns in eating.

29. A — An adult
   An adult helps prevent accidents.

30. C — They cook at the same time
   Equal pieces cook evenly.

31. D — Inward, away from the edge
   Handles sticking out can be knocked.

32. C — Germs and lice can spread
   Personal items should be for one person.

33. D — A toothbrush and toothpaste
   These clean teeth safely.

34. B — Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   A cloth mop works well.

35. A — Dusting
   Dusting removes dust from surfaces.

36. D — Mopping
   Mopping washes floors.

37. D — Rubbish or waste
   Refuse means waste.

38. A — Wash hands with soap
   Hands may carry germs.

39. A — Reuse containers
   Reuse cuts down rubbish.

40. D — So it does not pull through the cloth
   A knot anchors the thread.

SECTION B
----
41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Saves trees and forests, saves money, reduces smoke and illness, saves time looking for firewood.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each benefit.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Measuring gives correct stitch lengths, straight lines and correct size of the item.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the burn under cool running clean water for at least ten minutes, cover it loosely with a clean cloth and tell an adult.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Milk, beef, hides and skins, manure, or draught power (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each product.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Plastic and glass, because they do not rot.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two items, 1 mark for the reason.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Remove laces; brush off loose dirt; scrub gently with soapy water; rinse; stuff with paper; dry in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Calf, kid and lamb.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct name.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give vitamins, they give fibre and water, and they can be sold for money.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; bring the needle up; make 1 cm stitches with 1 cm gaps along the line; keep the thread loose; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

53. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.

54. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not mix chemicals; keep chemicals from children; wear gloves for dirty work; do not leave floors wet (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

55. (2 marks)
   Answer: Keeping the home and its surroundings clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for keeping clean, 1 mark for the home.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Passion fruit turns purple or yellow and wrinkles; guava turns yellowish and smells sweet; pawpaw turns yellow or orange and gives when pressed.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with fruit.

57. (4 marks)
   Answer: Cook with an adult; turn handles inward; use a dry cloth for hot pots; open lids away from the face; keep water away from hot oil (any four).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: The first hole is too big, so tie cloth around it or use a smaller hole. The other hole is blocked, so clear it gently with a thin wire.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for cause and fix for both holes.

59. (2 marks)
   Answer: The stitches are easy to see and to remove.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.
